This is really subtle. This is primarily an academic calendar. However,  the calendar image that appears to be embedded in the page, there is a block at the bottom center that starts with an underlined "Days of Classroom Instruction -147" In that block is an explicit statement of instructional *hours*. It's shows up in .txt, tesseract_raster, and tesseract_screenshot.

---
Days of Classroom Instruction ………………………………..147

High School Days 147 x 7.5 hrs. per day = 1102.5 hrs.
State Requirement = 1,050 hrs.
Elementary Days 147 x 7.25 hrs. per day= 1065.75 hrs.
State Requirement = 963.5 hrs.
---
This shows that each High school day is 7.5 hours and each elementary school day is 7.25 hours. From this, we should be able to derive that each high school day is 450 minutes and each elementary school day is 435 minutes. I'm unclear whether North Dakota or Dunseith Public School District 4M groups middle school with the elementary schools or the high schools (as middle school is typically categorized with high school as a secondary school).

The new three-tier busing schedule for the 2027-2028 school year will be:
High School (Tier 1): Start time at 7:35 AM and end time at 2:41 PM. The approved high school
schedule maintains the standard 84-minute course periods and 34-minute resource period. While the
total school day is shortened by eight minutes, this time is reclaimed by slightly reducing the passing
periods for the third block and lunch, ensuring no loss of instructional time.
Middle School (Tier 2): Start time at 8:10 AM and end time at 3:23 PM. This preserves the current
middle school length of day.
Elementary School (Tier 3): Start time at 9:00 AM and end time at 3:58 PM. The elementary schedule
delays the start time by 10 minutes and lengthens the school day by 5 minutes. Options to return the
school day to its current length will be considered as implementation plans are developed.
